images.text: Is there a specific way to request web pages? Absolutely, we can do that through URL encoding. It is a process in which is possible to transform characters into a specific format in order to transmit the data over the internet. A URL or a Uniform Resource Locator is the element that allows specifying the location of a computer network and the way to retrieve requests in a browser. URL’s work mainly with pages that use the HTTP protocol but we can also use it for file transfer (FTP), email (emailto) or database access (JDBC).

Are there any specifications to set a URL? Well, most of URL’s have to be displayed in an address bar above the webpage. They include basically three parts: a protocol, a hostname and a file name. For instance, if we have the site https://en.wikiloop.org/Uniform_Resource_example.html in that case the protocol will be https, the hostname “en.wikiloop.org”, and the file name “Uniform_Resource_example.html”

Are there different types of characters in URL encoding? That’s right. Servers and browsers can read and display different types of characters to ensure a universally accepted representation of data. There are mainly four types of characters. First, we have ASCII control characters, these are non-printing characters that we use for output control. They always include a code point or number within a character set. For instance, the number 127 is represented by the letters DEL. Then, we can also find Non-ASCII control characters, they make part of the ISO- Latin character set and they cover the set of characters beyond the ASCII character set of 128 characters.

In the third place, there are reserved characters. They make reference to special symbols such as comma, colon, semi – colon, forward slash, among others. As these types of characters may have different meanings in a URL, it is necessary to encode them.

Finally, there are some characters called unsafe because they can be misread within URL’s; for this reason, they also require encoding. The pound character or the percentage characters are examples of this type of symbols.

There is and There are in Questions
You use there is and there are to indicate that an object or a person is located in a specific place or to say that something exists.
Is there a reference to a web resource you know?
Is there a widely understood encoding for characters?
Is there a way to encode characters?

We use there is for singular uncountable nouns: 

There is only a way to solve this coding problem.

There isn’t any way to solve this coding problem.

Is there any way to solve this coding problem?

We use there are for plural countable nouns:

There are specific mechanisms to program a webpage.

There aren’t  specific mechanisms to program a webpage

Are there specific mechanisms to program a webpage?

To ask a question, we need to change the order of words in the sentence, this is the structure:

Is/Are + there + noun + complement?

Examples:

Is there an encoding language in URL?

Are there characters that need to be encoded in URL?
